subject: Comp band definitions + geo-localization approach for Q3 hiring
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Comp band definitions + geo-localization approach for Q3 hiring

Hi team —

We're locking compensation guidance for the Q3 hiring slate next week. I want to align on two quick things so we can finalize offer guardrails for recruiting and hiring managers:

1) Level definitions: small edits to L3/L4 responsibilities that came out of the calibration session — see bullets below.
2) Geo-localization: a proposal to move from a four-tier country band to a percentile-based differential for markets we frequently hire into.

Quick asks: can Laura and Neha share the most recent benchmark packet (market comps + percentiles) by EOD today? Karthik, can you confirm whether the current offer approval flow needs changes if we adopt percentiles rather than fixed bands? Jordan — please flag any payroll/offer system constraints.

Proposed next steps (fast path):
- Gather benchmarks and produce a one-page table mapping L2-L5 medians by market (Laura)
- Draft geo-differential formula (e.g., median * (1 + delta)) and share example offers (Neha)
- Confirm approval routing/time impact before announcing to recruiting (Karthik/Jordan)

I want us to avoid re-opening the entire band structure — this should be a definitional update with clear examples and a short FAQ for hiring managers.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: 2026-market-benchmarks.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Comp band definitions + geo-localization approach for Q3 hiring

Connor —

Sending the benchmark packet attached. Highlights from the data:
- US coastal markets (SF/NY): medians ~18-22% above national median for L3-L5 across our set of peer comps.
- Large APAC hubs: Singapore/Seoul cluster ~6-10% below US national medians but higher than broader APAC averages.
- Small markets (Eastern Europe/Latin America): medians vary widely; recommend capping offers at the 60th percentile to avoid long tails.

I've annotated the PDF with suggested guardrails and two exemplar offer tables for L3 and L4 in SF vs Bangalore. See pages 4–6.

I think a percentile-based approach will be cleaner for recruiters (pick target percentile per role/priority). That said, we should set hard caps for low-cost markets where total compensation could create internal equity issues.

I'll be on the 2pm comp sync; can walk through the tables and answer questions.

Laura Bennett
Director, Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: 2026-market-benchmarks.pdf (pdf)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Comp band definitions + geo-localization approach for Q3 hiring

Thanks Laura — packet looks solid. A few concrete recommendations from my side after modeling: 

- Geo-differential proposal (starter): apply percentiles to local medians, then a market multiplier with caps. Example: Offer = LocalMedian(role, level) * (1 + TargetPercentileDelta).
  - Priority hires (P0): 75th percentile target, up to +25% multiplier cap for highly constrained markets.
  - Standard hires (P1): 60th percentile target, up to +12% cap.
  - Low priority (P2): 50th percentile target, up to +8% cap.

- For internal parity, add a floor equal to the company national median for any role to avoid outliers.
- Recommend separate handling for equity: keep stock grant guidance unchanged; only base salary adjusts by geo differential initially.

I've put examples and the working sheet here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cQ3-market-benchmarks (tab: geo-proposal). The sheet includes modelled offer columns, total comp impact, and estimated annual run rate.

Action items:
- Laura: confirm market caps you'd be comfortable publishing by EOD Thurs (2026-07-02).
- Karthik & Jordan: review approval flow and payroll constraints and call out any blockers by Friday.
- Connor: we'll prepare a one-page FAQ and candidate FAQ for recruiters once caps are confirmed.

Neha Kapoor
Compensation Analyst
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: geo-differentials-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Mercury Compensation <partners@mercurycomp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Comp band definitions + geo-localization approach for Q3 hiring

Thanks for looping us in — we ran a quick methodological check on the packet and Neha's model. Key notes:

- Methodology: using local medians + percentile delta is standard and preserves local market signals. We recommend a 36-month lookback for benchmarking data to smooth transient peaks.
- Sample size note: for small markets (<25 datapoints) rely on regional proxies and add a 5% uncertainty buffer to the multiplier.
- Candidate negotiation friction: larger multipliers (20%+) materially increase counteroffer risk in coastal US; consider higher equity refresh options as an alternate lever.

Attached is a short memo on methodology and a recommended template for the hiring mgr FAQ. Happy to sync 30 minutes next week to finalize language.

Best,
Maya Patel
Senior Consultant, Mercury Compensation

[Attachment: mercury-methodology.pdf (pdf)]
